event.summary: Qualify the grid Shift+Enter single-write guarantee
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: The implementation specification promises that Shift+Enter reaches the terminal in one write even though the supported Mac implementation explicitly permits it to be split when the terminal input queue is nearly full. This overstates the guarantee future maintainers are told to preserve. Details: SPEC_impl.md:1722-1728 newly says the terminal host writes ESC CR to the pty in one write and that this single write is the promise. The encoder does produce one two-byte input (crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/grid_input.rs:298-313), but crates/terminal-host/src/host.rs:570-617 only offers the remaining bytes in one libc::write call and retains a short-write suffix for a later call. The terminal-host contract at crates/terminal-host/SPEC.md:399-403 explicitly says: An Input of at most ATOMIC_INPUT bytes is offered to the pty whole, in one write call; The pty may still take only part of it when its input queue is nearly full (macOS's pty takes what fits and returns a short write), and the rest then follows in later writes; How the program's reads divide the bytes is up to the program and its terminal settings; the host promises nothing about it. The revised root implementation spec should state the same offered-in-one-call guarantee and OS/read-boundary caveat. The original suspected consequence was Escape and Enter arriving separately at a boundary-sensitive line editor; the explicit lower-level contract accepts that PTY behavior, so this finding is the contradictory new documentation, not a request to change the terminal host. Suggested bucket: other (maintenance contract accuracy; no established user data-loss or security route). Confidence: confirmed by source and both contracts; no execution performed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none for the conflicting root wording; the terminal-host Input section accepts the actual partial-write implementation. Material caveat: the ordinary case and the encoder's one-message behavior are correct; only the unconditional guarantee is wrong.

event.summary: Qualify the grid Shift+Enter single-write guarantee
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Synthesis revision: retain the documentation-only finding; distinguish a single encoder message, an offer to libc::write, successful physical writes, and program read boundaries. TLDR: The new implementation explanation promises an unconditional single PTY write, although the terminal-host contract explicitly allows a short-write suffix to be written later. Future maintainers receive incompatible guarantees. Details: SPEC_impl.md:1722-1727 newly says the encoder sends ESC CR as one input, which the terminal host writes to the pty in one write, and states "The single write is the promise". One input is established by grid_input.rs:298-313; that does not establish one successful physical write. terminal-host/src/host.rs:573-580 explicitly describes offering the whole input initially, possible macOS short writes and no room-first wait. Its implementation at 591-617 writes segment.data[segment.written..], advances written by the returned count and retains a short-write suffix for a later call. The exact lower contract at crates/terminal-host/SPEC.md:399-403 is: "An `Input` of at most `ATOMIC_INPUT` bytes is offered to the pty whole, in one `write` call, so the host itself never
splits a key that encodes to several bytes (Shift+Enter's ESC CR). The pty may still take only part of it when its input
queue is nearly full (macOS's pty takes what fits and returns a short write), and the rest then follows in later writes.
How the program's reads divide the bytes is up to the program and its terminal settings; the host promises nothing about
it." SPEC.md:2869-2876 already contains the stronger product-level single-write/read-boundary motivation; the newly added root implementation wording repeats that stronger guarantee without reconciling it with the actual terminal-host contract. It is therefore an incorrect unconditional implementation explanation even though it is not a newly introduced end-to-end product requirement. Qualify the new text as offered whole in the initial write call, preserve the short-write and program-read caveats, and reconcile the existing product statement rather than treating a one-message encoder as proof of delivery atomicity. Original suspected consequence preserved: ESC and CR might reach a boundary-sensitive line editor separately, changing a newline chord into Escape-plus-submit. The lower-level contract explicitly permits the relevant PTY/read behavior; no runtime split, unintended submit, destructive command or loss-of-work sequence was observed or established. This record does not request a terminal-host code change and does not lower any previously established security/data-loss route (none was established). Suggested bucket: other, documentation contract accuracy. Could-be-highest: no established route; a destructive submit would require a concrete shipped input sequence and effect not shown by these source checks. Confidence: confirmed documentation contradiction and partial-write source path; user-visible split outcome is not verified. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none for the inaccurate new explanation; the terminal-host Input contract accepts the actual implementation. No runtime execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Clipboard queue may replace older pending copies under a slow sink
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: Considered whether the new shared clipboard-queue description conflicts with the promise to copy each completed selection, because a busy sink causes older pending values to be replaced. Source: the new wording at SPEC_impl.md:1730-1737 describes both selection and program-copy paths through one queue. crates/farhelm-ui/assets/clipboard-writer.js:1-63 has one in-flight write and one replaceable pending value. terminal.js:4326-4334 sends both system-clipboard program writes and local selections to this queue. Decision: do not report; the behavior is explicitly accepted by SPEC.md Terminal experience, the clipboard paragraph, whose exact relevant text is: "Clipboard operations are explicitly best-effort and silent on failure" and "A broken, hung or slow clipboard is not something Farhelm adds complexity to support well: copies may be dropped while it is in that state, but nothing else in Farhelm may stall because of it." The source queue implements that bounded nonblocking behavior; no new defect in its replacement policy was established. Could-be-highest: no; clipboard contents are expressly excluded from loss-of-user-owned-work severity by review_feedback_queue/AGENTS.md Priority buckets, and no credential read or other security route is involved here. Suggested bucket if retained: other. Confidence: confirmed source/spec acceptance; no execution. proposed_drop: the exact SPEC.md clipboard acceptance quoted above. possible_cover: that specification rule only; no other coverage sources searched.

event.summary: Clipboard queue may replace older pending copies under a slow sink
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Synthesis revision: retain the proposed exclusion as narrowly about replacing pending clipboard writes, with exact acceptance and queue limits. TLDR: When a clipboard operation is still outstanding, additional copy requests may supersede an older pending value instead of each reaching the sink. Considered whether the new queue description conflicts with every-completed-selection copying; the explicit slow-clipboard exception accepts this consequence. Source: SPEC_impl.md:1729-1734 newly describes a page-wide queue. terminal.js:4326-4334 routes system-clipboard program writes and completed local selections through enqueueClipboardWrite. clipboard-writer.js:22-59 starts one operation, retains one replaceable pending value, and starts that pending value only when the prior operation resolves, rejects or throws. It does not wait in the selection/parser caller. An indefinitely pending operation holds that slot indefinitely; continued copies only replace the one pending value. The limit established here is one in-flight operation plus one pending value, not a proof of a byte limit inside this helper. Exact specification acceptance at SPEC.md:3075-3080: "Clipboard operations are
  explicitly best-effort and silent on failure — permission policy, secure-context requirements, and an engine's own
  clipboard behavior are outside this system's control — a deliberate, named exception to the Errors and diagnostics
  section's surface-every-error rule below, not a lapse in it. Farhelm assumes the host's system clipboard works. A
  broken, hung or slow clipboard is not something Farhelm adds complexity to support well: copies may be dropped while
  it is in that state, but nothing else in Farhelm may stall because of it." The three-copy case where the middle pending value is superseded is the original suspected consequence; this revision preserves it and does not claim every accepted enqueue reaches the sink. Decision: proposed exclusion unchanged because the exact named exception permits copies to be dropped while the sink is slow or hung, and this helper keeps unrelated processing nonblocking. Suggested bucket if retained: other. Could-be-highest: false; this is clipboard-value replacement only, which Priority buckets excludes from loss of user-owned work; no read/disclosure claim or credential route is made. Confidence: confirmed source/spec acceptance, not execution. proposed_drop: SPEC.md Terminal experience 3075-3080, exact text quoted above. possible_cover: only that specification rule; no forbidden coverage sources searched. Parent has not accepted this proposed exclusion. No tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: The shared control font rule preserves the grid input's terminal typeface
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Release the middle button while the primary remains held: onDocumentMouseUp:1666-1674 reports that middle release but keeps the replacement gesture because ev.buttons is nonzero. A later primary-held move passes 1657-1658 without suppression; the primary release passes 1670 because ending.withheld is now false. That release also has ending.link=null, so 1689-1693 does not activate the originally pressed link. grid-input.js:508-517 recognizes these buttons and maps primary-held motion to button 0; 555-559 admits releases and dragged motion, and 575-584 deduplicates only repeated moves. The supervisor does not restore ownership: grid_input.rs:688-745 encodes valid primary Up and held Move directly for ordinary SGR click/drag modes. No reproduction or runtime incidence is claimed; this is the conditional source path through the shipped event handlers.
